description: Domain-agnostic fact extraction prompt using structural types (ValueType, PropertyType, slot_name)

system_messages.content:
Extract ATOMIC facts from documents. Each fact is ONE claim with a subject, predicate, and object.

For each fact, classify its STRUCTURAL TYPE using three dimensions:

1. VALUE_TYPE (what kind of object/value is being asserted):
   - NUMERIC: Numeric quantities with optional units (35 mph, $2,000, 3 people, 70%, 10 kg)
   - TEMPORAL_POINT: A single point in time (March 5, 2023; 5:30 p.m.; 2021)
   - TEMPORAL_INTERVAL: A duration or time range (for three hours, from 2018 to 2020, during the past 10 years)
   - LOCATION: Places, addresses, or geographic/physical locations (New York City, Berlin, 123 Main St, second-floor hallway)
   - BOOLEAN: A yes/no or presence/absence fact (seatbelt was worn, no prior accidents, product was not recalled)
   - CATEGORICAL: Discrete labels, types, roles, statuses, or classifications (clear weather, red light, full-time, gold tier, critical severity)
   - ENTITY_REF: A reference to another entity (person, organization, product, case, vehicle, system). Use the exact name/ID from resolved_entities when possible (Maria Lopez, ACME Corp, Server A, Building 2).
   - TEXT: Free-form descriptive text when nothing else fits (long descriptions, explanations, quotes). Use TEXT only as a fallback if no more specific VALUE_TYPE applies.

2. PROPERTY_TYPE (what kind of relationship is expressed between the subject and the value):
   - TEMPORAL: When something happened or how long it lasted (occurred_on, occurred_at, started_at, ended_at, lasted_for, was_valid_during)
   - QUANTITATIVE: Magnitudes, amounts, counts, or rates (traveled_at_speed, had_amount, had_count, had_score, weighed, cost_amount)
   - LOCATION: Where something was or where it occurred (was_at, occurred_at, lived_in, headquartered_in, stored_at)
   - ATTRIBUTE: Types, categories, states, conditions, or statuses (is_type, has_role, has_color, had_state, had_status, was_injured, had_severity)
   - RELATION: Roles and relationships between entities, including identity/equivalence (is_employee_of, is_owner_of, is_member_of, represents, is_parent_of, is_same_person_as, is_supplier_for)
   - EXISTENCE: Whether something existed, occurred, or was present/absent (occurred, existed, was_present, did_not_occur, was_not_present)
   - MODALITY: Obligations, permissions, abilities, requirements, or possibilities (must_pay, is_required_to, is_allowed_to, can_do, could_access, must_not)

3. slot_name (which "slot" of the subject this fact is filling):
   - A short, generic, snake_case label that names the property being asserted.
   - Examples: "speed", "incident_date", "employment_status", "payment_amount", "event_location", "primary_physician", "product_recall", "outage_duration", "environment_description".
   - Do NOT include entity names or specific values in slot_name. It should describe the kind of property, not the particular instance.

RULES:
- Each fact must be ATOMIC: exactly one subject–predicate–object claim per fact.
- Extract DENIALS as facts ("has not been involved in prior accidents" -> is_denial: true, PROPERTY_TYPE often EXISTENCE or ATTRIBUTE or RELATION depending on what is being denied).
- Skip obvious legal boilerplate or generic template language (e.g., standard prayers for relief, jurisdictional recitations) and mark them as is_boilerplate: true if extracted.
- When an event or condition is clearly about the main incident under discussion, set temporal_context: "current_incident".
- When an event is clearly about past incidents or history, set temporal_context: "prior_incident".
- Use exact entity names (and IDs if provided) from resolved_entities for subjects and ENTITY_REF values whenever possible.
- Prefer non-TEXT VALUE_TYPE when any specific type applies (NUMERIC, TEMPORAL_POINT, TEMPORAL_INTERVAL, LOCATION, BOOLEAN, CATEGORICAL, ENTITY_REF). Use TEXT only as a last resort.
- Facts should be concise: keep the "text" field under ~30 words.
- Output valid JSON only.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "node_type": "STATED_FACT",
      "id": "STATED_FACT_0",
      "text": "<fact under 30 words>",
      "value_type": "<VALUE_TYPE>",
      "property_type": "<PROPERTY_TYPE>",
      "slot_name": "<short snake_case label for this property>",
      "value_raw": "<exact value text from document>",
      "assertion_triple": {
        "subject": "<subject entity or noun phrase>",
        "relationship": "<predicate_raw, e.g. traveled_at_speed>",
        "object": "<object/value phrase>"
      },
      "certainty": "0.95",
      "temporal_context": "current_incident",
      "is_denial": false,
      "is_boilerplate": false,
      "temporal_validity": {
        "t_valid_from": null,
        "t_valid_until": null
      },
      "metadata": {}
    }
  ],
  "edges": []
}

COMMON PREDICATES (examples only, NOT a closed list):
- TEMPORAL: occurred_on, occurred_at, started_at, ended_at, lasted_for, was_valid_during
- QUANTITATIVE: traveled_at_speed, cost_amount, had_amount, had_count, had_score, weighed
- LOCATION: was_at, occurred_at, headquartered_in, lived_in, stored_at
- ATTRIBUTE: is_type, has_role, has_color, had_state, had_status, had_condition, had_severity
- RELATION: is_employee_of, is_owner_of, is_member_of, represents, is_parent_of, is_supplier_for, is_same_person_as
- EXISTENCE: occurred, existed, was_present, did_not_occur, was_not_present
- MODALITY: must_pay, is_required_to, may, may_not, can_do, could_access, must_not

Use clear, descriptive predicates that match the natural language meaning; these predicate examples are suggestions, not strict requirements.

examples.segments: The blue sedan driven by Alex Rivera was traveling at approximately 45 miles per hour.

nodes.text: The blue sedan was traveling at 45 miles per hour.

examples.segments: Since 2021, Priya has been working full-time at Northwind Analytics.

nodes.text: Priya is employed full-time at Northwind Analytics.

examples.description: Service outage duration (TEMPORAL_INTERVAL + TEMPORAL, slot_name = outage_duration)
examples.segments: The service outage lasted for three hours.

nodes.text: The service outage lasted for three hours.

examples.segments: The annual conference took place in Berlin, Germany.

nodes.text: The annual conference took place in Berlin, Germany.

examples.description: Product recall denial (BOOLEAN + EXISTENCE, slot_name = product_recall, is_denial = true)
examples.segments: The AlphaX heater has never been recalled.

nodes.text: The AlphaX heater has never been recalled.

examples.segments: Dr. Smith is the primary physician for Ellen Lee.

nodes.text: Dr. Smith is the primary physician for Ellen Lee.

examples.description: Contractual payment obligation and amount (MODALITY + BOOLEAN, QUANTITATIVE + NUMERIC)
examples.segments: Under the agreement, Brightline Media must pay a licensing fee of $50,000.

nodes.text: Brightline Media is obligated to pay a licensing fee.

examples.description: Free-text environment description (TEXT + ATTRIBUTE, slot_name = environment_description)
examples.segments: The hallway was cluttered with boxes and loose cables.

nodes.text: The hallway was cluttered with boxes and loose cables.
nodes.value_raw: cluttered with boxes and loose cables

assertion_triple.subject: hallway
assertion_triple.object: cluttered with boxes and loose cables
